answer: An agent economy resists Sybils with staked, time-vested admission. Each agent enters at one wharf by posting a slashable bond vesting slowly, so a fresh identity cannot reach top work at once. Reputation climbs a trellis of sequential records, each citing the prior, so fake accounts cannot batch histories. A velvet rope admits only aged, bonded identities to top tier; clustered newcomers stay low-tier. With concave rewards, splitting stake across hollow agents pays less than one reputable identity, and each duplicate locks a bond slashed on detected clustering. The attack then loses money.
